sovereign_country.strategic_role: 苏伊士运河经济特区、辐射中东及北非的低成本轻工制造

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Oversized Furniture and Home Decor

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Greater Arab Free Trade Area (GAFTA) Agreement
Agadir Agreement (Egypt, Jordan, Tunisia, Morocco; in force 2007)
Egypt-UK Bilateral Investment Treaty (1975, continued post-Brexit)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing, as amended, and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 15 of 2003, as amended); Companies Law No. 194 of 2020 and Ministerial Decree No. 904 of 2021 promulgating its Executive Regulations; GAFI Beneficial Ownership Register instructions; EFCU (Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit) AML/CFT directives implementing FATF Recommendations 24 and 25.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of shareholders'/UBOs' passport (each natural person)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country notary public and competent Ministry of Foreign Affairs

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate shareholder
Bank reference letter confirming source of funds for each UBO contributing capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Egyptian incorporation counsel/notary
UBO declaration form and beneficial ownership register initial filing sheet
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: GAFI Beneficial Ownership Register (Egyptian notary/GAFI one-stop-shop)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, shareholders, directors, managers, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list (for USD correspondent/remittance clearing), EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK OFSI list, and the Prosecutor-General's terrorism designation list maintained by EFCU. Enhanced due diligence is statutorily required for foreign and domestic politically exposed persons (PEPs), including their family members and close associates, pursuant to Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended and EFCU directives. Ongoing transaction monitoring and event-driven rescreening apply after incorporation; cash and wire threshold reporting obligations continue per EFCU instructions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Investor Services Center online portal and one-stop-shop (General Authority for Foreign Investment), linked to the Ministry of Trade and Industry Commercial Registry system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official company name must be registered in Arabic script in conformity with the Companies Law No. 194/2020 and its Executive Regulations. A Latin-script transliteration may be recorded as a supplementary notation, but the Arabic name is authoritative for the Commercial Register. The transliteration must follow the phonetic Arabic rendering of the foreign name and must not create confusion with any existing registered Arabic name or a protected trademark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 days of the rejection notification, the applicant must file a written administrative objection at the same GAFI one-stop-shop, accompanied by the reservation receipt, supporting trademark registrations, prior-use evidence, and any explanatory correspondence. GAFI's Legal Review Committee will issue a determination within 10 working days. If the administrative review affirms the rejection, the applicant may, within 60 days of service of the final administrative decision, file a formal appeal with the Administrative Court of the Council of State, contesting the name refusal under the Companies Law and the Executive Regulations.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible. Egyptian law requires the LLC to maintain a real head office in Egypt recorded in the Commercial Register for service of process, statutory notices, and tax communications. A virtual office may be used as a communications or administrative service address in addition to, but not in lieu of, a verifiable physical location. For an online oversized furniture and home decor retailer intending to hold stock, at least one leased storage or fulfillment premise, or a co-located administrative space, must be disclosed to GAFI and the Egyptian Tax Authority.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate. Estimated annual risk of unannounced on-site inspection at approximately 15% for an LLC with no direct import activity. The probability rises to approximately 30% if the entity declares warehoused imported goods, owing to customs and VAT verification priorities; port-of-entry customs examination of oversized cargo remains mandatory.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: GAFI online name reservation and Commercial Registry filing fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Law No. 194 of 2020 and its Executive Regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the Memorandum of Association and notarial registration
Publication of incorporation notice in the Official Gazette and a licensed commercial newspaper
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian Official Gazette (Waqa'i' al-Misriyya) and licensed press

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Register establishment certificate and extract
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Trade and Industry – Commercial Registry

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization / apostille of three foreign-issued documents (passport copies, Power of Attorney, Certificate of Good Standing or bank reference letter)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Egyptian consulate (if consular legalization path)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per document under the Hague Apostille Convention and prevailing consular fee schedules

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Arabic translation of apostilled or legalized foreign documents
Licensed Egyptian counsel flat fee covering pre-incorporation due diligence, drafting the Memorandum of Association, filing the Power of Attorney, and registry representation
Corporate bank account KYC/beneficiary verification charge, if imposed by the chosen bank
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial bank (e.g., Commercial International Bank, Banque Misr)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018 and Executive Regulations No. 96 of 2018, Articles 6-19 and Executive Regulations Articles 139-172 (Limited Liability Companies); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 (one-stop shop provisions); E-Commerce Law No. 180 of 2018 (online retail provider registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registry One-Stop Shop, operating with the Ministry of Trade and Industry Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Model Articles of Association and Notice of Incorporation (GAFI Form) issued under Executive Regulations No. 96 of 2018, resulting in the Certificate of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to LLCs under Executive Regulations 96/2018; stated capital of EGP 1,000 to EGP 10,000 is accepted for e-commerce activities. Cash contributions must be paid into the corporate bank account within 30 days of incorporation; no escrow account or bank certificate is mandatory. In-kind contributions must be fully transferred at formation and supported by a notarized valuation report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription of the Founders to the fully paid share capital of the Company, as recorded in the Articles of Association, is hereby ratified and accepted. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the premises located at [address, governorate, Egypt] shall be the registered office and statutory seat of the Company, and all legal notices may be served at that address. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [name, passport number] is appointed General Manager and [name, national ID] Chief Financial Officer, each authorized, jointly or severally, to sign banking documents, execute commercial contracts, and file statutory declarations before GAFI, the Commercial Registry, and the Egyptian Tax Authority. RESOLVED, that the corporate seal is adopted, and the officers may procure duplicates thereof.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop – Electronic Services Portal (Cairo/Smart Village Investor Service Center)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the name reservation request online or in person, proposing three alternative names. Select the ISIC 4791 activity descriptor for e-commerce retail of furniture and home décor. Pay the statutory fee, obtain the Name Clearance Certificate, and receive a provisional incorporation file number.
required_dossiers: Name clearance application with three proposed names
Copy of passport or national ID for each proposed shareholder
Power of attorney if a formation agent acts on behalf of any founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or conflict, submit an alternate name from the pre-registered slots. If an administrative query is raised, respond within 10 business days through the same portal and provide amended name declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Notary Department / Ministry of Justice Notary Office within the One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the GAFI model Articles of Association before the notary, acknowledging the stated capital, shareholder identities, and share allotments. Authenticate signatures physically or via the approved electronic signature platform. Ensure the registered office address is stated in the formation contract.
required_dossiers: Model Articles of Association (GAFI standard form) with Name Clearance Certificate reference
Original passports or national IDs of all subscribing shareholders
Original notarized power of attorney, if a representative signs
Lease contract or title deed evidencing the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary cannot complete authentication because of incomplete shareholder identification, have the omitted shareholder execute a ratification deed and re-book a notary slot. Requests for corrections must be filed with the same GAFI file number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing and Issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation application with the notarized Articles, the lease evidence, and the fee payment receipt. The GAFI registry verifies statutory compliance, issues the Certificate of Incorporation, assigns the CAPMAS statistical number, and automatically triggers Commercial Registration and tax identification data in the unified records.
required_dossiers: Completed GAFI Notice of Incorporation application
Notarized Articles of Association
Notarized lease contract for the registered office
Receipt of the official state filing fee payment
Copy of name clearance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or formal objection, remedy the stated discrepancy within the statutory cure period (usually 10 business days). For missing documents, upload supplementary filings online; for contested activity codes, submit the ISIC 4791 supporting description of oversized furniture e-commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration and CAPMAS Statistical Number Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Trade and Industry – Commercial Registry (Trade Register), governorate branch via GAFI automatic issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the Commercial Registration Extract automatically generated by GAFI reflects the primary activity code ISIC 4791 and the registered warehouse address. If physical files are required for customs or bank purposes, collect the certified extract from the governorate Commercial Registry office and update the warehouse or showroom branches separately.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
GAFI-issued incorporation file
Notarized board resolution appointing the responsible signatory
Lease contract of the registered office and any additional warehouse
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registration Extract contains a wrong activity code, file a rectification request with the Commercial Registry and append the ISIC 4791 definition. A response should issue within 5 business days; escalate to GAFI's aftercare department if the registry remains silent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Tax Card Issuance, and E-Invoice Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – local tax office and e-Invoice portal under the Unified Tax Procedures Law No. 206 of 2020
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Tax Card at the competent ETA office. Register for Value Added Tax if taxable supplies exceed the statutory threshold, and activate the ETA e-Invoice system for B2B and B2C transactions. Disclose the e-commerce channel, including cross-border payment settlements via Stripe and Affirm BNPL, and provide the bank account certificate for the new corporate account.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Commercial Registration Extract
Corporate lease contract
Certificate of bank account opening or bank statement
Notarized board resolution listing the authorized tax signatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Tax Card is not issued within the SLA, request an interim Tax Card under the Unified Tax Procedures Law and file a complaint at the ETA one-stop shop. Repeated delays may be escalated to the ETA grievance committee with a written notice and proof of physical submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Official Gazette and Chamber of Commerce Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official Gazette (Al-Waqaa' Al-Misriyya) and the governorate Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: GAFI transmits the incorporation abstract to the Official Gazette for publication. Confirm the gazette issuance and pay the publication fee. Register the newly formed LLC with the governorate Chamber of Commerce and obtain the membership certificate, which is commonly requested by banking counterparts and e-commerce payment processors.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Commercial Registration Extract
Certified copy of the Articles of Association
Proof of payment of publication fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette notice is missing or contains inaccuracies, submit a written correction request to GAFI's registry department to obtain an amended attestation for publication. For Chamber of Commerce rejection, provide additional copies of the notarized lease and board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Payment Rails Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian bank (e.g., Commercial International Bank, Banque Misr, HSBC Egypt) under Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) e-commerce merchant regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the corporate bank account in the company's name, complete Know Your Customer and Ultimate Beneficial Owner forms, and submit the board resolution confirming the signatories. Instruct the bank to enable merchant settlement functions for international e-commerce payment processors, which facilitates subsequent approvals for Stripe and Affirm BNPL settlement via a local acquiring partner.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Commercial Registration Extract
Tax Card and VAT registration certificate, if issued
Notarized board resolution for bank signatories
Passport copies of all signatories
UBO declaration forms
Approved lease contracts for the principal place of business
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the account without additional corporate documents, request a certified true copy from GAFI and re-submit. If the bank declines support for international payment processor settlement, apply to a bank licensed by the CBE for e-wallet and e-payment merchant acquiring services.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Trade and Industry – Industrial Development Authority (IDA) for warehouse and assembly annexes; primary online retail activity falls under the Commercial Registry and the General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC) only if physical import/export of furniture is conducted.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Registration Certificate (ISIC 4791 – Non-Store E-Commerce Retail of Home Furniture) under E-Commerce Law No. 180 of 2018, together with the Civil Defense Occupancy Permit for the oversized-furniture warehouse.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B (gray list) – Simplified Environmental Review and registration via the EEAA unified EIA portal for warehouse/logistics facilities; full Category C EIA Report is triggered only if in-house upholstery, wood finishing, or coating workshops are established.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If backup generators or HVAC systems are installed, comply with EEAA Decree No. 44 of 2000 combustion-source emission limits and maintain ambient PM10 below 50 ug/m3. Wastewater discharges to public sewer must meet Law No. 93 of 1962 requirements (pH 6-9, BOD5 not exceeding 300 mg/L, COD not exceeding 450 mg/L, TSS not exceeding 350 mg/L). Packaging waste, damaged furniture returns, and cardboard must be segregated and consigned to EEAA-registered recyclers under Waste Management Law No. 202 of 2020; open burning is strictly prohibited.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Fire Safety Permit for the warehouse and any showroom, requiring annual inspection, fire extinguishers, evacuation signage, and approved storage layout for oversized furniture racks. A structural load/storage clearance from the municipal engineering directorate is required for high-bay racks. Under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003, the employer must file an occupational health registration with the Ministry of Manpower, provide first-aid and evacuation plans, and for staff above 15 persons appoint a health and safety coordinator and register an internal fire team with the General Administration of Civil Defense.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; e-services portal at www.eta.gov.eg (also electronic invoice portal at https://www.eta.gov.eg/en/ElectronicInvoicing)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Because non-resident ownership is permitted, the LLC first registers as a juridical person with the Commercial Registry and obtains a unified tax card (United Tax Number / TIN) from the competent Tax Directorate. For VAT identification, the LLC must file an ETA VAT registration application via the ETA's online portal within 60 days of exceeding the registration threshold, appoint a tax representative if a non-resident is concerned, and obtain a VAT certificate. The TIN is mandatory for customs clearance, import/export declarations, and e-invoicing enrollment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not permit check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity elections. An LLC is mandatorily taxed at entity level; no partnership pass-through election is available. A group may apply for consolidated tax filing for wholly-owned subsidiaries only if the Finance Minister authorises it under the Income Tax Act, but this does not alter entity-level classification. Corporate income tax is 22.5%.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Egyptian VAT Law No. 67 of 2016 and amendments
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supply value; once registered, monthly returns and e-invoicing obligations apply regardless of subsequent turnover
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt mandates near-real-time electronic invoicing ('e-invoice') and electronic receipts ('e-receipt') for VAT-registered persons. Businesses must integrate with the ETA's Invoice Clearance Platform using certified JSON/XML schemas and a token-based HTTPS API. Every invoice must be signed with a private key and receive a unique QR code / fiscal stamp from ETA before issue. The ETA performs real-time schema validation, duplicate detection and duty/quantitative checks; non-integrated sales or rejected invoices trigger monetary penalties, freezing of VAT refunds and suspension of registration.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under article 23(1) of Egyptian VAT Law, goods physically exported outside Egypt are zero-rated when the supplier retains evidence of customs clearance and release from Egypt, payment of freight/insurance if sold under CIF terms, export shipping documents, and actual receipt of foreign currency proceeds credited to an Egyptian bank account in accordance with Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) regulations. Offshore services sold to a non-resident and effectively performed outside Egypt may be zero-rated if the service is physically connected to abroad and the recipient is outside Egypt. The LLC must record sales as zero-rated only at the time the physical shipment has left Egyptian customs territory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (outward manifest / SAD code for export release)
Bill of Lading or similar proof of shipment (or air waybill for air freight)
Inward Remittance Certificate made out to the exporting LLC and issued by the collecting Egyptian bank
Signed Commercial Invoice and Packing List evidencing consignment, container number and HS classification relevant to oversized furniture retail
Certificate of Origin (when required by the destination country or letter of credit)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA field audits may demand re-verification of customs release data against the customs system and CBE foreign-currency receipts. If a zero-rated export is unsupported, the input VAT apportioned to that export is clawed back and assessed at the 14% VAT headline rate, plus late-payment interest, delay and non-compliance fines of up to EGP 100,000 per violation; intentional fraud or fictitious export documentation additionally triggers criminal prosecution under the VAT Law (imprisonment and fine), disqualification from e-invoicing and denial of future refunds. Retrospective assessment reaches back five years from the date of filing and may extend to ten years where fraud is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — the exclusive monetary authority and foreign-exchange regulator, exercising powers under Banking Law No. 194 of 2020, Payment Systems Law No. 18 of 2019 and the CBE's Rules of Dealing in Foreign Currencies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Egyptian Pound (EGP) is convertible on the current account: Egypt has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations, allowing unrestricted payments for trade in goods and services, dividends, interest and profit repatriation without CBE pre-approval. The capital account is managed: foreign direct investment (share capital and shareholder loans), EGP-denominated foreign investment and portfolio flows must be channelled through licensed banks with mandatory CBE statistical reporting. A flexible, but managed, exchange-rate regime operates post-December 2022, with interbank market pricing and no formal rationing. Profit remittance by an Egyptian LLC to a foreign parent is lawful provided the bank holds the statutory supporting file: tax card and tax clearance, audited financial statements, board distribution resolution and CBE-declared underlying transaction documents. Practical friction arises when USD liquidity is tight, prompting enhanced due-diligence queues on high-value wires and strict verification of logistics/import documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: 100% of export proceeds must be received into the Egyptian banking system within five (5) months from the date of shipment, per CBE instructions to banks. Mandatory conversion ratio: 0% — exporters are not obliged to convert receipts into EGP; proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency accounts and used for bona fide trade, service payments or other permitted current transactions. Failure to repatriate within the statutory timeline exposes the exporter to bank-imposed compliance restrictions, possible suspension of trade-finance facilities and adverse CBE enforcement on the bank and the customer.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multicurrency account (EGP/USD/EUR) with dedicated trade-finance and treasury sub-limits
Operational account (EGP/USD) plus capital-deposit sweep account for shareholder capital injection
Operational account (EGP/USD) with import-settlement and FX-forward sub-limit
Operational account and corporate treasury FX-hedging account (deliverable forwards)
Operational account (EGP/USD) for cross-border payment settlement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: LOW–MEDIUM. Offshore digital EMIs (EU/UK e-money licences, digital-only banks) are not authorised to provide payment services, hold EG-persian funds or issue EGP IBANs to Egyptian residents without a CBE licence under Payment Systems Law No. 18 of 2019 and CBE e-money regulations. Such EMIs may only be used as auxiliary rails for outbound non-EGP disbursements (e.g., settling overseas logistics or supplier invoices from segregated foreign-currency balances), never for inbound export receipts, local merchant settlement or EGP clearing. Onshore licensed payment fintechs are commercially viable for e-commerce acquiring (including Stripe-style flows), but they do not replace the bank as the clearing node for trade payments and FX conversion.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for corporate account opening. Authorised signatories and all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) must attend an in-person due-diligence interview at the bank branch in Egypt presenting original passports, the notarised Arabic-translated incorporation certificate, tax card, memorandum and articles of association, UBO register and a board resolution establishing the signatory mandate. Remote video onboarding is generally not accepted by tier-1 Egyptian banks for initial corporate KYC. At least one principal signatory and attributable UBO must appear physically; foreign-resident additional signatories may be appointed by power of attorney notarised and legalised through Egyptian consular channels, with a certified Arabic translation, but on-boarding cannot proceed wholly remotely.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce merchant profile combining high cross-border transaction volume with refund, chargeback and BNPL (Stripe/Affirm) settlement flows, creating a structuring or unauthorised-payment-processing red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed merchant agreements with Stripe and Affirm; platform ownership and domain registration; business plan and financial projections; refund/chargeback policy and historical chargeback ratios; transaction-monitoring and AML programme documentation; marketing and logistics counterparty contracts; tax card and tax payment evidence; letter CPA-reviewed financial statements for the first operating years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ownership by a non-resident high-net-worth individual or with Politically Exposed Person (PEP) exposure under Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended) and CBE AML/CFT regulations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP declaration signed by each owner/signatory; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence (tax returns, asset records, bank reference letters); certified passport and residence permit copies; current shareholding register; clean criminal-record certificate; board CVs; and a local AML opinion from Egyptian counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Oversized-furniture trade requiring disbursements to multiple foreign factories and freight/logistics providers inconsistent with declared business volume or invoiced values.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master supply agreements and proforma invoices; value-certified commercial invoices; Egyptian customs import declarations including the mandatory ACID (Advance Cargo Information Declaration) numbers; freight-forwarding and carriage contracts; bills of lading or air waybills; delivery confirmation and inspection certificates; carrier payment instructions; and bank reference letters for first-time suppliers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a jurisdiction with enhanced-risk classification or through an opaque multi-tier ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group authorisation hierarchy and board minutes approving the capital increase; full organisational chart down to natural-person ultimate beneficial owners; transcripts of incorporation in the parent jurisdiction; audited consolidated financial statements of the ultimate parent; tax residence certificates and economic-substance documentation; a notarised legal opinion on the transaction from Egyptian counsel; and a detailed purpose-of-funds letter describing how the capital will be used for furniture import and logistics.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Share capital injections and shareholder loans must be routed by SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank intermediation) through a licensed Egyptian bank. The remitter must specify the purpose as 'FDI equity subscription' or 'Shareholder loan disbursement' with the CBE statistical-reporting code for direct investment; the receiving Egyptian bank issues a foreign-capital transaction credit advice and reports to the CBE. Verifiable documentation includes the LLC board resolution approving the capital increase, GAFI electronic filing and registration evidence, amended articles of association filed with the commercial registry, and the parent entity's audited financials showing the source of funds. Any conversion of USD/EUR into EGP is executed at the interbank rate at the licensed bank; no CBE pre-approval is required for genuine direct investment under the current liberalised regime. The funds must be used strictly for the declared business purpose to avoid reinvestment/remittance restrictions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for oversized furniture imports use SWIFT MT103 for single-invoice payments, referencing the importer tax card, the GAFI import registration number and Egypt's ACID customs identifier. Large-amount or recurring purchase orders are settled by Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) or documentary collection (MT400/MT422) with title-document accompaniment. Logistics and freight for oversized consignments are paid as trade-related service transfers under SWIFT MT103 supported by freight-forwarding contracts, charter-party bills of lading, customs release declarations and evidence of completed import. All outbound payments are verified against underlying trade documentation and the bank's CBE export-repatriation and import-compliance monitoring obligations; payment to third-country suppliers without full import documentation may be treated as capital outflow and rejected.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (USD/EGP and EUR/EGP) with substantiated underlying trade invoices and bank-approved tenors.
Cross-currency swap agreements (USD/EGP, EUR/EGP) used to hedge operating cash-flow and asset-liability mismatches.
FX option structures (USD/EUR-call or EGP-put) supported by documentary evidence of committed trade exposure.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) instruments: generally not permissible for onshore Egyptian-resident hedging; only non-resident counterparties may access offshore NDF markets, and any such arrangement must not be booked through the Egyptian banking system.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Commercial Registry Office (Ministry of Justice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of the initial registration date; application window is the 30 days preceding the expiry date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs statutory surcharges under Commercial Registry Law 34/1976; continued non-renewal leads to suspension, removal of the legal entity status, and administrative strike-off of the commercial register record.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements Submission under Companies Law 159/1981
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (December 31), i.e., no later than June 30 of the following year, coinciding with the mandatory Annual General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of EGP 5,000–20,000 for non-submission or filing of incomplete statements; persistent default may trigger dissolution proceedings initiated by GAFI.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of the fiscal year-end, i.e., by April 30 for a December 31 year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing addition of up to 2% of the tax due per month, with a minimum of EGP 500; unreported tax liability is increased by 5% per year of delay and may be compounded.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Register Confirmation and Shareholding Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI in coordination with the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit for AML compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation within 30 days after the anniversary of the initial UBO register filing date and within 14 days of any shareholding transfer or beneficial ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties under AML Law 80/2002 for inaccurate or stale UBO records; repeated violations result in fines up to EGP 500,000 and temporary suspension of managerial registrations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all Egyptian LLCs; no small-company exemption exists under Companies Law 159/1981. Each LLC must appoint at least one certified external auditor regardless of size, revenue, or number of shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which fully align with IFRS, issued by the Ministry of Finance and enforced by GAFI and ETA; public-interest entities apply full IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a beneficial ownership register identifying any individual holding more than 25% ownership or effective control. Annually, the LLC must re-confirm its shareholding structure with GAFI. Every share transfer or change in UBO must be documented in the Minutes Book and filed with GAFI within 14 days to keep the statutory registers accurate and current.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday. Under Investment Law No. 72/2017, eligible projects in least-developed governorates may deduct up to 50% of investment costs from taxable profits; Free Zone projects are exempt from income tax but pay an annual 1% goods-traffic fee; small and micro entities with annual turnover below prescribed thresholds may elect the simplified turnover tax regime at 0.5%–2.5% under Law No. 152/2020.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 8 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) electronic portal (inatax.gov.eg), with the annual Transfer Pricing Disclosure Form attached as required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return, supplemented by quarterly provisional tax installments during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and final tax settlement are due within four months after the close of the fiscal year; a taxpayer with a December 31 year-end must file and pay by April 30 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total worldwide sales gross of returns and discounts, including online furniture sales settled via Stripe, Affirm BNPL, bank transfers, and cash on delivery.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident LLC without Egyptian permanent establishment (PE) does not file Form 8; the Egyptian counterparty or payment facilitator must apply applicable withholding. If a PE exists, full Form 8 filing applies through an appointed tax representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Oversized-furniture inventory costs, customs duties, inbound freight, warehousing, and direct fulfillment labor.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CEGS and deductible costs must be substantiated via invoices and customs declarations; foreign parent imports into Egypt must be valued on an arm's length basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing, platform fees, payment processing fees, logistics, insurance, depreciation, and allocated head-office administrative charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management and technical service fees paid to non-residents are deductible only if documented and subject to 20% withholding; excessive fees are subject to transfer pricing adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual TP disclosure of controlled transactions with foreign parent, logistics providers, and group service companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be completed even where no formal Local File threshold is met if aggregate controlled transactions exceed EGP 5 million; failure triggers separate fines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Taxable Income and Tax Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from accounting profit to taxable profit after statutory add-backs and deductions, applying the 22.5% headline rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PE's taxable profit must be computed under the same rules using Egyptian GAAP and the ETA's deemed-rate assumptions where records are inadequate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 – Tax Credits, Provisional Payments, and Balance Due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carryforward of losses (maximum 5 years), foreign tax credits, quarterly provisional installments, and any remaining balance payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No foreign tax credit is available to a non-resident without PE; the final balance must be settled by the filing deadline to avoid monthly surcharges.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment attracts a surcharge of 2% per month or part of a month on the unpaid tax; late filing exposes the taxpayer to discretionary administrative penalties and automatic assessment by the ETA; wilful non-filing is treated as evasion and referred to criminal prosecution. A tax clearance certificate cannot be issued until all filings and payments are settled.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% – imposed as a final tax on the Egyptian distributing LLC rather than a classic shareholder withholding; economically borne by the shareholder and payable by the company at distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced rate under an applicable Double Taxation Agreement (DTA), the foreign shareholder must deliver to the LLC and the ETA (i) a Certificate of Tax Residence issued by the home-state tax authority, legalized or apostilled with an Arabic certified translation, (ii) a completed ETA beneficial ownership declaration confirming the shareholder has economic substance and entitlement to treaty benefits, and (iii) supporting distribution resolutions and bank records. Reduced rates apply at the moment of distribution; if the statutory 10% tax was already borne, the shareholder must file a refund claim with the ETA within the five-year prescriptive period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for IP and know-how: 20% statutory, generally reduced to 10%–15% under DTAs. Interest on cross-border loans and credit facilities: 20% statutory, generally reduced to 10%–15% under DTAs. Technical, management, and consultancy fees paid to non-residents: 20% statutory, with treaty relief available subject to substance and DTA formalities.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when a single controlled transaction with a related party exceeds EGP 10 million, or when aggregate annual related-party transactions exceed EGP 30 million; Master File is required when group-wide consolidated revenues exceed EGP 15 billion; an annual TP disclosure form must be submitted with the Form 8 return where aggregate controlled transactions exceed EGP 5 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply the Gulf Cooperation Council 'Economic Substance Regulations', but the ETA applies general anti-avoidance, beneficial ownership, and PE attribution principles under Law No. 91/2005 as amended. A paper-only Egyptian LLC whose online retail operations, decision-making, and oversized-furniture fulfillment are in substance carried on outside Egypt may be disregarded or treated as a conduit, with income re-attributed to the foreign parent and treaty benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Diverting Stripe or Affirm BNPL receipts to personal or foreign bank accounts, understating gross furniture sales, issuing fake refunds, or destroying delivery manifests to reduce taxable income in the Form 8 return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 2% per month on unreported tax, plus criminal fines; wilful evasion under Articles 133–136 of Law No. 91/2005 is punishable by imprisonment of 3 to 5 years and fines of up to EGP 1 million, together with confiscation of goods and mandatory publication of the judgment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or knowingly approve off-book sales face joint civil liability for unpaid tax, personal criminal imprisonment, administrative seizure of personal assets, and travel bans pending full settlement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Egyptian LLC solely to hold a payment gateway while actual management, purchasing, and oversized-furniture logistics are fully executed outside Egypt; issuing invoices without a genuine Egyptian office, staff, or inventory.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA may disregard the LLC as a sham, disallow intercompany deductions, recharacterize income as attributable to the foreign parent's Egyptian PE, levy a deemed-profit assessment, and impose monthly delay surcharges plus double penalties for abusive structuring.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the full tax shortfall under veil-piercing rules, subjected to precautionary attachment of bank accounts and moveable assets, and banned from leaving Egypt until tax clearance is issued.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare and submit the Local File / Master File when thresholds are met, failure to file the annual TP disclosure form, or concluding related-party warehouse, logistics, and platform fees at non-arm's length prices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of up to EGP 500,000 for documentation failures; discretionary ETA transfer pricing adjustments increasing taxable income; additional tax at 22.5% plus the 2% monthly delay surcharge; potential double taxation absent timely MAP/APA action.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve deliberately false TP documentation face criminal charges for providing false information to the ETA, personal fines, and imprisonment for up to 3 years in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating high-volume Stripe and Affirm BNPL collections without merchant-of-record AML due diligence, commingling corporate receipts with personal accounts, structuring deposits to avoid banking thresholds, or processing refunds to third-party cards to launder proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sanctions under Egypt's Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80/2016 as amended include confiscation of laundered proceeds, fines of up to EGP 2 million, and imprisonment of 7 to 30 years for organized laundering practices; the E-Commerce unit and banking system may permanently blacklist the merchant.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who knowingly facilitate payment-rail laundering face personal criminal prosecution, unlimited civil restitution to affected parties and the state, travel restrictions, and disqualification from acting as directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax and Profit Repatriation Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to the foreign parent without paying the 10% final dividend tax, or repatriating profits through undocumented management fees, inflated royalties, or fictitious loans to avoid the statutory 20% withholding on services and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unpaid withholding tax is recovered at 20%–22.5% of the gross remittance with the 2% monthly surcharge; false deduction of such payments triggers a 100% add-back; CBE exchange-control reporting violations lead to delayed, blocked, or revoked repatriation approvals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve unlawful repatriations are jointly and severally liable for the withholding tax and surcharges, may face precautionary seizure of their assets, and can be criminally prosecuted for aiding the unlawful outward transfer of Egyptian funds.
